68.label: Unanswered: False Coin in the Cattle Market
68.desc: The trail went cold. Aeltje Vos walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

171.label: Band: The Velvet Knives
171.desc: Sworn together by Aeltje Vos, Neeltje Imhoff, Ottilie Vos, who all walked from you. They feed the Vendetta every week. Go in Disguise to build a case against them.

187.label: Unanswered: Fire at the Tanner Warehouse
187.desc: The trail went cold. Aeltje Vos walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

190.label: Fire at the Pietersz Warehouse
190.desc: The bucket-chain got there in time to save the walls and nothing else. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. The Carolina says the Fire for whoever did. (The Warrens)

192.label: Abroad: Barbel Nagel
192.desc: Barbel Nagel walked out of the Blood Court smiling. They were innocent, and now they hate you.

196.label: Ursel Vos
196.desc: Ursel Vos, a known fire-setter. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg. (Accused in: Fire at the Pietersz Warehouse)

201.label: Matthes Visscher
201.desc: Matthes Visscher, the building's owner. Has had a key to the house for years. (Accused in: Fire at the Pietersz Warehouse)

204.label: Unanswered: Protection in Adornes Lane
204.desc: The trail went cold. Aeltje Vos walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

215.label: False Coin in the Cattle Market
215.desc: The false coin is being passed at every tavern on the Harbour, always to strangers. The Mintmaster wants the die; the Council wants a name. On the passer, when the passer was nearly taken: a purse with two compartments. (The Harbour)

219.label: The Market
219.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

235.label: A purse with two compartments
235.desc: Dropped in the scramble. It leads somewhere.

236.label: Wouter Pauw
236.desc: Wouter Pauw, a discharged soldier. Has had a key to the house for years. (Accused in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

237.label: The Harbour
237.desc: Quays, the great crane, bonded warehouses and foreign sailors. Everything here is for sale, including silence.

238.label: Beadle Kürschner
238.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

239.label: Partial: The Mould Read
239.desc: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

242.label: Old Offender: Griet Claesz
242.desc: Old Offender. 4 crimes on the record. Smokes a clay pipe of cheap Dutch tobacco, one bowl after another.

243.label: No Forced Entry
243.desc: Not a mark on the locks. Whoever came in had a key, or was let in by someone who trusted them.

244.label: Apollonia Barker
244.desc: Apollonia Barker, a moneychanger. Has ink-black fingers; works a printer's press. (Accused in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

246.label: Always the Same Way
246.desc: always to strangers. A passer has habits, and habits are a face.

247.label: Cicely Fletcher
247.desc: Cicely Fletcher, a tavern-keeper. Wears civet and rosewater, like a courtier. (Accused in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

teammate.label: Beadle Pfister
teammate.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

252.label: Witness: Magdalena Bakker
252.desc: Magdalena Bakker, the Mintmaster's assayer. Saw something near the Cattle Market, and has something of their own to hide. (Witness in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

257.label: Protection in Hobson Lane
257.desc: Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Hans Schmidt's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. (The Stews)

259.label: Witness: Lienhard de Witt
259.desc: Lienhard de Witt, a boy who sells kindling. Saw something near the Cattle Market, and has heard there is a reward. (Witness in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

263.label: Burglary at Pfister the Goldsmith's
263.desc: Anneke Tanner came down at prime to find the back shutter open and the strongbox empty. It was not a crocheteur's work, but it was not a nervous man's either. (The Market) The Bishop asks mercy for whoever did this, if they repent: a Pardon or a Fine, not the rope.

teammate.label: Apothecary's Boy Nagel
teammate.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

journal.title: Week 26
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. The broadsheet-sellers count the thieves abroad, and sing the number in the Market. Griet Claesz has done it again: Burglary at Pfister the Goldsmith's. Anselm Vogt spoiled a token of yours. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 4 open; 11 Coin in hand.

journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Cattle Market. You find: A Plaster Mould, A purse with two compartments. The first name on the board: Wouter Pauw. The case takes you to The Harbour.

journal.title: The Rope: Aeltje Vos
journal.text: Aeltje Vos hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. Their band drinks to them in a cellar and to you in a different tone. The Bishop's chaplain will remember that you were asked.

journal.title: Sleep

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: Guilty: Aeltje Vos
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Aeltje Vos is convicted of Burglary at Bicker's Pawnshop, and the judge breaks his staff. Their name comes off the wall. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Bess Welser presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.title: Condemned: Aeltje Vos
journal.text: Aeltje Vos goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea, The Guild's Plea.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 22
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. The broadsheet-sellers count the thieves abroad, and sing the number in the Market. Anselm Vogt spoiled a token of yours. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 13 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Wounded
journal.text: Someone was waiting on the stair of your lodging. You remember the first blow of the cudgel and not much after.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. The false coin is being passed at every tavern on the Harbour, always to strangers. The Mintmaster wants the die; the Council wants a name. On the passer, when the passer was nearly taken: a purse with two compartments.

journal.title: Taken: Aeltje Vos
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Aeltje Vos, a receiver from the Market. It has to be.

journal.title: A Watchman Hurt
journal.text: Beadle Pfister was set upon outside the Watch-house. They will be in the Abbey hospital for a while.

journal.text: Anselm Vogt has closed Protection in Adornes Lane with a confession the Provost is pleased with. The Council notes who was quicker.

journal.text: The hand is familiar. Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Nan Hobson's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

journal.title: They Found Each Other
journal.text: Aeltje Vos, Neeltje Imhoff, Ottilie Vos: every one of them walked away from one of your cases. Now they drink in the same cellar, and call themselves the Velvet Knives.

journal.title: Guilty: Griet Claesz
journal.text: The sworn men are out for two days. Griet Claesz is convicted of Fire at the Kessler Warehouse, and the judge breaks his staff. On half proof the Court convicts of the lesser crime only: a careless fire, not arson. The case closes, and a small fee comes with it. At the court door Caspar Barker presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. Anselm Vogt spoiled a token of yours. The ledger: no case closed; 3 open; 9 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Scene Spoiled
journal.text: Somebody has been at Partial: The Oil Named before you could use it: moved, wiped, muddled. Anselm Vogt's people were seen in the lane.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. Somebody in the city has a furnace going on Sunday, when the forges are cold: sacks of charcoal carried in at night. The Mintmaster is certain of the die. In a midden nearby, a crucible with silver in the cracks.

journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Anselm Vogt closed a case of yours first. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: 1 case gone cold; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Answered by the Rival
journal.text: Anselm Vogt has closed False Coin in the Cattle Market with a confession the Provost is pleased with. The Council notes who was quicker.

journal.title: The Trail Goes Cold
journal.text: False Coin in the Cattle Market goes into a box in the basement. Somewhere in The Market, Aeltje Vos hears the crier and laughs.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. The bucket-chain got to the Kessler Warehouse in time to save the walls, at matins. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. A witness saw a man watching from across the road, not running. In the strongbox, unburnt: a lease near its end.

journal.title: The Provost's Examiner
journal.text: Anselm Vogt has the Provost's letter and a desk on the other side of the Market. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.
